title: Information foraging
relevance: Founding statement of information foraging theory, information scent and ACT-IF; basis for treating index entries as scent and sources as patches.

title: Information Foraging in Information Access Environments
relevance: Gives Holling disc equation, patch model with MVT condition, diet model and zero-one rule applied to Scatter/Gather; formal basis for stopping and source-class exclusion rules.

title: Optimal foraging, the marginal value theorem
relevance: Original marginal value theorem: leave a patch when marginal gain rate equals habitat average rate; theorem underlying agent patch-leaving rule.

title: The Marginal Value Theorem (lecture notes, Bio 608)
relevance: Textbook derivation of the MVT optimality condition B'(C)=B(C)/C and second-order condition used in the notes' proof.

title: SNIF-ACT: A Cognitive Model of User Navigation on the World Wide Web
relevance: Formal information-scent equations (PMI-based activation, softmax link choice) and validation (R2 .69-.91 link choice, .73-.80 backing up); basis for writing index cues.

title: Discretionary task interleaving: heuristics for time allocation in cognitive foraging
authors: Stephen J. Payne; Geoffrey B. Duggan; Hansjörg Neth
relevance: Empirical evidence that people approximate MVT with rate-sensitive and giving-up-time heuristics; template for agent stopping heuristics.

title: An Analysis of Theories of Search and Search Behavior
relevance: Formal comparison of IFT, search economic theory and iPRP within one framework; links foraging to formal models of search behaviour.

title: Information Scent, Searching and Stopping: Modelling SERP Level Stopping Behaviour
relevance: Shows SERP-level scent stopping rules improve simulated gain and fit real behaviour; supports scent-based stop rules for agents.

title: Searching and Stopping: An Analysis of Stopping Rules and Strategies
authors: David Maxwell; Leif Azzopardi; Kalervo Järvelin; Heikki Keskustalo
relevance: Frustration-point and disgust stopping rules best match real searchers; candidate stopping rules for agent loops.

title: Scent of Knowledge: Optimizing Search-Enhanced Reasoning with Information Foraging
relevance: InForage: RL reward with information-gain and efficiency terms inspired by IFT; shows how foraging is (and is not) operationalized in LLM search agents.

title: SCOUT: Active Information Foraging for Long-Text Understanding with Decoupled Epistemic States
authors: Zhenliang Zhang; Wenqing Wang; Yong Hu; et al.
relevance: Applies active information foraging with gap diagnosis toward query sufficiency; up to 8x token reduction; agent analogue of ASK and stopping by sufficiency.

title: PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
relevance: Formulates web collection as patch-switching foraging under a budget; direct agent application of patch model.

title: Information Farming: From Berry Picking to Berry Growing
relevance: Argues GenAI shifts users from foraging/berrypicking to cultivating information; frames KB compilation as farming.

title: Revisiting Human Information Foraging: Adaptations for LLM-based Chatbots
authors: Sruti Srinivasa Ragavan; Mohammad Amin Alipour
relevance: Argues IFT must be re-validated in non-patchy chatbot environments; caution on transferring IFT to LLM agents.

title: Supporting Business Document Workflows via Collection-Centric Information Foraging with Large Language Models
authors: Raymond Fok; Nedim Lipka; Tong Sun; Alexa Siu
relevance: Collection-centric foraging with schemas over document collections; 16% faster tasks (n=16); relates to typed extraction over collections.

title: Over-Searching in Search-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Roy Xie; Deepak Gopinath; David Qiu; et al.
relevance: Quantifies over-searching and proposes Tokens Per Correctness; currency for foraging-style stop rules.

title: To Search or Not to Search: Aligning the Decision Boundary of Deep Search Agents via Causal Intervention
authors: Wenlin Zhang; Kuicai Dong; Junyi Li; et al.
relevance: Shows over/under-search from misaligned sufficiency thresholds; empirical counterpart of patch-leaving decisions.

title: Is Progressive Disclosure All You Need for Long-Context Agents?
authors: Yifeng He; Yinzhe Zhao; Jicheng Wang; Hao Chen
relevance: Controlled study: one-level progressive disclosure helps at scale, second level hurts; interpreted via MVT travel-cost reasoning.

title: Dissecting Agentic RAG: A Component Ablation for Multi-Hop QA with a Local 7B Model
relevance: Two retrieval iterations capture 95% of the gains of five; evidence for short berrypicking loops.

title: Frustratingly Easy Agentic RAG via Portable Skills: A Case Study in Customer Support
authors: Istok Bako; Bonan Min; Tiffany Shao; Claire Cheng; Yashar Mehdad
relevance: Wikipedia-style navigation layer over SOPs; 83.3% evidence sufficiency; link between scent/index design and sufficiency evaluation.

title: The design of browsing and berrypicking techniques for the online search interface
relevance: Berrypicking: evolving queries, bit-at-a-time retrieval and six search techniques; maps to agent tool repertoire and iterative loop.

title: A behavioural approach to information retrieval system design
relevance: Ellis's behavioural characteristics (starting, chaining, browsing, differentiating, monitoring, extracting); maps to agent tools and filters.

title: Models in information behaviour research
relevance: Nested model of information behaviour/seeking/searching and synthesis of Ellis, Kuhlthau, Belkin, Dervin; organizes seeking models for agent loop design.

title: Inside the search process: Information seeking from the user's perspective
venue: Journal of the American Society for Information Science 42(5):361-371
relevance: Information Search Process model with uncertainty; basis for redundancy-based stopping and exploration-dip calibration.

title: Information Search Process (ISP) model page
relevance: Author's statement of ISP stages, feelings/thoughts/actions, validation studies and the principle of uncertainty.

title: ASK for information retrieval: Part I. Background and theory
authors: Nicholas J. Belkin; Robert N. Oddy; Helen M. Brooks
relevance: Anomalous State of Knowledge hypothesis: needs cannot be fully specified; supports gap-driven retrieval and clarification.

title: Question-negotiation and information seeking in libraries
relevance: Four levels of information need (visceral, conscious, formalized, compromised); theoretical basis for the agent clarify step.

title: The language of information need: Differentiating conscious and formalized information needs
relevance: Empirical test of Taylor's levels via linguistic patterns; suggests automated detection of when to clarify.

title: Exploratory search: from finding to understanding
relevance: Lookup/learn/investigate taxonomy; basis for routing between typed lookups, navigation and iterative search.

title: Asking Clarifying Questions in Open-Domain Information-Seeking Conversations
authors: Mohammad Aliannejadi; Hamed Zamani; Fabio Crestani; W. Bruce Croft
relevance: Qulac dataset; one good clarifying question gives >170% P@1 (oracle); quantitative support for clarify step.

title: Relevance: A review of the literature and a framework for thinking on the notion in information science. Part II: nature and manifestations of relevance
relevance: Stratified manifestations of relevance (system, topical, cognitive, situational, motivational/affective); maps to layered agent evaluation.

title: Framing Relevance for Safety-Critical Autonomous Systems
relevance: Reproduces Cooper's formal minimal-premise-set definition, Saracevic's strata table and Mizzaro's 4D framework; source for formal relevance definitions.

title: A definition of relevance for information retrieval
relevance: Logical relevance via minimal premise sets; formal precursor of sufficient context and minimal citation sets.

title: Situational relevance
relevance: Extends logical relevance with situation, stock of knowledge and goals; justifies novelty and task-based evaluation.

title: The concept of relevance in IR
relevance: Multidimensional, dynamic relevance; situational relevance as most realistic for interactive evaluation; informs agent retrieval evaluation.

title: Relevance: The whole history
relevance: History of relevance research and the four-dimensional framework including time; supports temporal applicability metadata.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Hailey Joren; Jianyi Zhang; Chun-Sung Ferng; Da-Cheng Juan; Ankur Taly; Cyrus Rashtchian
relevance: Operational sufficient-context definition and autorater; failure to abstain on insufficient context; LLM-era counterpart of logical relevance.

title: Perspectives on Large Language Models for Relevance Judgment
authors: Guglielmo Faggioli; Laura Dietz; Charles Clarke; et al.
relevance: Human-machine collaboration spectrum and cautions on LLM relevance judges; informs calibrated judges for KB evaluation.

title: Large language models can accurately predict searcher preferences
authors: Paul Thomas; Seth Spielman; Nick Craswell; Bhaskar Mitra
relevance: LLM relevance labels as good as human labellers at Bing; prompt sensitivity; evidence for LLM judges in golden-set evaluation.

title: Colon Classification (CC)
venue: Knowledge Organization 44(4):291-307; ISKO Encyclopedia of Knowledge Organization
relevance: PMEST facets, canons (exhaustiveness, exclusiveness, helpful sequence) and CC's decline; basis for mapping envelope facets and hard-filter safety conditions.

title: Facet analysis
venue: ISKO Encyclopedia of Knowledge Organization (preprint of IP&M article)
relevance: Defines facet analysis and critiques its a priori rationalism; argues for empirically derived facets.

title: ISO 25964 - the international standard for thesauri and interoperability with other vocabularies
relevance: Scope of ISO 25964-1/-2 and mapping to SKOS (closeMatch, exactMatch, compound equivalence gap); standard behind alias tables.

title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
relevance: Normative SKOS label and relation semantics (one prefLabel per language, broader not transitive); lint rules for concept units.

title: The Structure of Collaborative Tagging Systems
authors: Scott A. Golder; Bernardo A. Huberman
relevance: Tag proportions stabilize after ~100 bookmarks (Polya urn); polysemy/synonymy problems; evidence on folksonomy vs controlled vocabulary.

title: What have we got to lose? The effect of controlled vocabulary on keyword searching results
relevance: 35.4% of keyword hits would be lost without subject headings; strongest empirical evidence for alias/controlled-vocabulary channel.

title: The vocabulary problem in human-system communication
authors: George W. Furnas; Thomas K. Landauer; Louis M. Gomez; Susan T. Dumais
relevance: P(two people choose same term) < 0.2; unlimited aliasing gives several-fold improvement; justifies altLabel lists and scent-rich index cues.

title: Faceted metadata for image search and browsing
authors: Ka-Ping Yee; Kirsten Swearingen; Kevin Li; Marti Hearst
relevance: 90% of 32 users preferred faceted metadata interface; usability evidence for facet navigation.

title: FRBR: Functional Requirements for Bibliographic Records (factfile)
relevance: Summary of FRBR user tasks, Work/Expression/Manifestation/Item and relationships; model for version chains and duplicates.

title: IFLA Library Reference Model: A Conceptual Model for Bibliographic Information
authors: Pat Riva; Patrick Le Bœuf; Maja Žumer
relevance: Consolidated FRBR/FRAD/FRSAD model (Res, WEMI, Agent, Nomen, Place, Time-span); target model for KB version/supersession relations.

title: IFLA Library Reference Model (LRMoo resources page)
relevance: Confirms LRM authorship/date and its linked-data formalization (LRMoo).

title: The concept of a work in WorldCat: an application of FRBR
authors: Rick Bennett; Brian F. Lavoie; Edward T. O'Neill
venue: Library Collections, Acquisitions, and Technical Services 27(1):45-59
relevance: 78% of works have one manifestation, ~6% complex works, metadata inheritance gains; quantifies where version machinery pays.

title: Information as thing
relevance: Retrieval systems store only information-as-thing; epistemic basis for evidence store with verbatim spans.

title: The wisdom hierarchy: representations of the DIKW hierarchy
relevance: Shows textbook consensus on DIKW definitions but not on transformation processes; critique of layered compile pipelines.

title: The knowledge pyramid: a critique of the DIKW hierarchy
relevance: Logical critique: information (FOL) cannot be inferred from data (existential-conjunctive); argues rules must be sourced, not induced from records.

title: Visions of Xanadu: Paul Otlet (1868-1944) and Hypertext
relevance: Otlet's monographic principle (decompose books into unit cards linked by UDC); historical precedent for atomic knowledge units.

title: Zipf's word frequency law in natural language: A critical review and future directions
relevance: Formal Zipf/Zipf-Mandelbrot statement, near-Zipfian fit, split-sample estimation and mechanism non-identifiability; basis for long-tail corollaries.

title: Zipf's Law Leads to Heaps' Law: Analyzing Their Relation in Finite-Size Systems
authors: Linyuan Lü; Zi-Ke Zhang; Tao Zhou
relevance: Derivation of Heaps from Zipf with finite-size refinement validated on 35 datasets; basis for vocabulary-growth reasoning.

title: Heaps' law
relevance: Heaps/Herdan formula V=Kn^beta, typical parameters and pointers to formal derivations; vocabulary/index growth.

title: Speculations on browsing, directed searching, and linking in relation to the Bradford Distribution
relevance: States Bradford's 1:n:n^2 law and maps core/middle/periphery to browsing/directed search/linking; justifies index+hybrid+links design.

title: Bradford's Law of Scattering: Ambiguities in the Concept of 'Subject'
relevance: Shows Bradford results depend on operationalizing 'subject' (words, concepts, task-useful items); caveat for scattering estimates.

title: An empirical examination of Lotka's law
relevance: 48 datasets conform to x^n y=c but only 7 to inverse square; evidence on author-productivity skew and parameter estimation.

title: Power Laws in the Information Production Process: Lotkaian Informetrics
relevance: Unifies Lotka, Zipf, Mandelbrot, Leimkuhler and Bradford as equivalent power laws; basis for Zipf-Lotka exponent mapping.

title: A general theory of bibliometric and other cumulative advantage processes
relevance: Cumulative advantage (modified Polya urn, Beta function) as mechanism for Bradford/Lotka/Zipf; explains rich-get-richer usage signals.

title: Emergence of scaling in random networks
relevance: Preferential attachment generates scale-free networks; generalizes cumulative advantage to link graphs.

title: Large Language Models Struggle to Learn Long-Tail Knowledge
authors: Nikhil Kandpal; Haikang Deng; Adam Roberts; Eric Wallace; Colin Raffel
relevance: QA accuracy tracks pre-training document counts; retrieval mitigates long tail; links Zipf tails to need for KB retrieval.

title: When Not to Trust Language Models: Investigating Effectiveness of Parametric and Non-Parametric Memories
authors: Alex Mallen; Akari Asai; Victor Zhong; Rajarshi Das; Daniel Khashabi; Hannaneh Hajishirzi
relevance: PopQA: LMs fail on less popular facts, scaling does not fix the tail; adaptive retrieval for tail queries.

title: Heads and tails: studies of web search with common and rare queries
authors: Doug Downey; Susan Dumais; Eric Horvitz
relevance: Search engines perform worse on rare queries; empirical tail difficulty for query distributions.

title: Source Coverage and Citation Bias in LLM-based vs. Traditional Search Engines
authors: Peixian Zhang; Qiming Ye; Zifan Peng; Kiran Garimella; Gareth Tyson
relevance: 55,936 queries: LLM search engines cite more diverse domains (lower Gini), Wikipedia 41% of Gemini citations, readability/structure predict selection.

title: Synthetic Sources?: Auditing Generative Search Engine Citations for Evidence of AI-Generated Sources
relevance: Per-engine top-25 share and Gini (0.49-0.65); 59.1% of domains cited once; ~16% AI-generated sources; source concentration in AI search.

title: AI Search Citations: How Much Do They Really Change Week to Week?
relevance: Vendor-reported: top 1% of domains hold 64% of AI citations; 96.8% week-over-week stability; concentration evidence (unaudited).

title: A Dynamic Theory of Organizational Knowledge Creation
relevance: SECI tacit/explicit conversion model; vocabulary for converting tacit SOP knowledge.

title: Conceptualizing Knowledge Creation: A Critique of Nonaka's Theory
relevance: Finds no SECI mode supported by evidence not explicable more simply; limits on tacit-to-explicit automation.

title: Organizational Learning and Communities-of-Practice: Toward a Unified View of Working, Learning, and Innovation
relevance: Canonical vs noncanonical practice: manuals omit actual work; argues for mining tickets/cases beyond SOP documents.

title: KCS v6 Practices Guide: Introduction / benefits
relevance: KCS demand-driven capture as by-product of work; foundation for KB curation operating model.

title: KCS v6 Practices Guide: The Double Loop Process
relevance: Solve/Evolve loops, capture in workflow, reuse is review, requestor's context; maps to single/double-loop learning and alias harvesting.

title: Chris Argyris: theories of action, double-loop learning and organizational learning
authors: Mark K. Smith (infed), summarizing Argyris & Schön 1978
relevance: Single- vs double-loop learning (Argyris & Schön 1978); analogy for KCS Solve/Evolve loops and schema evolution.

title: Beyond Accuracy: What Data Quality Means to Data Consumers
authors: Richard Y. Wang; Diane M. Strong
relevance: 15 data-quality dimensions in 4 categories from consumer surveys; separates storable intrinsic metadata from query-time contextual quality.

title: ISO/IEC 25012 Data Quality Model (overview)
relevance: ISO/IEC 25012 inherent vs system-dependent data quality characteristics; schema for KB quality metadata.

title: ISO/IEC 25012: Data Quality Model (arc42 quality model page)
relevance: Lists named ISO/IEC 25012 characteristics (accuracy, completeness, consistency, currentness, credibility, availability, confidentiality, compliance, traceability).

title: Data quality assessment
authors: Leo L. Pipino; Yang W. Lee; Richard Y. Wang
relevance: Functional forms for data-quality metrics (min aggregation, timeliness from currency/volatility); basis for review_due formula.
